children: PurMinds signed a 5-year collaboration with SpectroChip and Kaohsiung Municipal Siaogang Hospital to support clinical validation of its SwiftLab point-of-care diagnostics, subject to IRB and regulatory approvals. SpectroChip will provide NT$3M (~$94K) in research funding over five years.
Signals strategic push to validate POC tech in clinical settings.
Adds tech and clinical research capacity, de-risking development.
Provides modest, committed support for studies and training.
Revenue from clinical use in US/Canada not imminent.
Creates structure for studies and potential commercialization.

This is an early-stage strategic collaboration aimed at building clinical evidence for PurMinds’ SwiftLab POC platform. A catalyst would be positive clinical performance data followed by regulatory clearances enabling commercial deployment.
